Nema for Meeting preparation

Walk into the meeting with the open questions already organized.

Turn the calendar event and permitted notes into a focused meeting brief. Nema organizes what matters for this conversation while the meeting owner chooses the agenda.

All use cases ↗

Anchor the brief to the event

Start with the calendar details or a supplied event summary. Confirm the date, time, timezone, meeting owner, participants, and stated purpose. If an email address or name does not clearly match the account, ask for confirmation before adding personal or company research.

The meeting type sets the scope. A discovery call, technical review, procurement discussion, and renewal planning session each need different context and outcomes.

Select relevant account history

Give Nema access only to the notes and discussion appropriate for the meeting team. Ask it to pull the recent commitments, unresolved questions, and decisions that bear on this event. A long company profile belongs in account research. The meeting brief should include only what helps this group use the scheduled time.

Dates and authors matter. If a requirement came from an old note or a person who will not attend, keep that provenance visible. The account owner can decide whether to confirm it again.

Build an agenda around decisions

An agenda is more useful when every section has a purpose. Nema can propose an order, time allowance, owner, and intended outcome for each topic. For example, five minutes to confirm success criteria is clearer than a generic "goals" item.

The brief should distinguish questions to ask the customer from internal points the sales team needs to settle first. It can also flag an agenda that tries to cover more than the available time.

Review before the meeting

Post the draft in the deal Slack thread. The account executive checks participant roles, removes sensitive internal commentary, and chooses the final questions. A technical specialist can add the evidence they need, while the meeting owner confirms what must be decided.

Nema can revise the brief after that discussion. It does not send the agenda or invite participants unless a separate approved workflow grants that action.

Try the workflow tomorrow

Pick one meeting with a clear purpose and a small participant list. Provide the event details and the last relevant account update. Ask for a one-page brief and inspect every note it uses. After the meeting, compare the brief with what the team actually needed and refine the guidance for the next event type.

Questions from sales teams

Can Nema see every calendar event?

Access depends on the apps and permissions configured for the requester. Supplying the event details directly is a clear way to begin.

Will it invent an agenda owner?

It should leave the owner blank and ask when the source does not name one. The meeting owner confirms all assignments.

How is this different from account research?

Meeting preparation focuses on one scheduled conversation. It uses account context selectively to shape that meeting's agenda, questions, and decisions.
